issues.sym: Misfires, a rough or stumbling idle, hesitation when you press the gas, and a check engine light. It often shows up after rain, a car wash, or a coolant leak.
issues.why: The LT1 uses a front-mounted Optispark distributor that sits low behind the water pump. Moisture and coolant can get inside it and upset the ignition signal.
issues.next: Have the ignition system and the area around the water pump checked. Many owners replace the unit with a better-vented design, and any water pump leak above it should be fixed at the same time.

issues.sym: Coolant drips at the front of the engine, the temperature gauge climbs, and in bad cases white exhaust smoke or a milky oil cap.
issues.why: The LT1 does not tolerate heat well, and leaks from the water pump or hoses can lead to overheating and a failed head gasket.
issues.next: Stop driving if the gauge reaches hot. Have leaks found and fixed early, before the engine overheats.

issues.sym: The low-coolant light flickers or stays on even though the coolant is full.
issues.why: The coolant level sensor on these cars is touchy and commonly fails, giving false warnings.
issues.next: Check the coolant level with the engine cold first. If it is full, have the sensor tested and replaced.

issues.t: Seat belt retractor may not meet standards (recall)
issues.sym: Usually nothing you can notice; a belt may not lock or retract as it should.
issues.why: A small batch of cars was built with seat belt retractors that did not meet the federal standard.
issues.next: Run your VIN through a recall check and have the retractors replaced if the car is listed.

issues.t: Slow, noisy or failed power windows
issues.sym: Windows move slowly, scrape or rattle, or stop working.
issues.why: The window motors and regulators on this generation wear out, and the regulator rivets can break.
issues.next: Have the motor and regulator checked. Replacing the worn part usually fixes it.

issues.sym: Water drips inside around the roof panels, wet carpets or a stained headliner after rain or washing.
issues.why: The rubber seals around the removable T-top panels shrink and harden with age.
issues.next: Have the T-top seals inspected and replaced, and dry the interior to stop mold and electrical problems.

issues.sym: Tail lights, brake lights or turn signals are dim or work only some of the time.
issues.why: The rear bulb sockets and their connections corrode and loosen with age.
issues.next: Have the sockets checked and replaced, ideally on both sides, so other drivers can see you brake and signal.

issues.t: Weak welds near the driver door hinge (recall)
issues.sym: Usually nothing you can notice in normal driving.
issues.why: Welds near the lower driver-side door hinge may not have been made to spec, which could weaken the body in a crash.
issues.next: Check your VIN for this recall. Dealers add structural rivets to fix it.

issues.sym: Check engine light with timing codes such as P0008 or P0017, a rattle at startup, a rough idle or misfire, and loss of power.
issues.why: The timing chains on the early 3.6L V6 can stretch early, and long gaps between oil changes speed it up.
issues.next: Have the codes read and the chain checked soon. A badly stretched chain can jump and damage the engine. Keep oil changes on time.

issues.sym: A steady ticking from the engine, a misfire on one cylinder, and a check engine light.
issues.why: The special lifters used to shut off cylinders for fuel economy can stick or collapse. Left alone, a bad lifter can wear out the camshaft.
issues.next: Have it diagnosed promptly when a tick and misfire appear. Fixing a lifter early can prevent damage to the camshaft.

issues.t: Knee can knock the key out of Run (recall)
issues.sym: The engine shuts off while driving, often after the driver's knee bumps the flip key. Power steering and power brakes go away.
issues.why: The flip-style key sits where a knee can push it out of the Run position. GM recalled 2010-2014 cars and later recalled replacement flip keys sold for 2010-2015 cars.
issues.next: If it happens while you're driving: turn on your hazard lights, hold the wheel firmly and steer to a safe spot off the road. Steering and brakes can feel much heavier when the engine or power cuts out, so press the brake harder than normal. Have it checked before you drive it again. Check your VIN for both recalls. The dealer swaps the flip key for a fixed-blade key.

issues.sym: A power-height-adjustable front seat suddenly drops down.
issues.why: A shoulder bolt on the seat height adjuster can fall out.
issues.next: Check your VIN for the recall and have the bolts replaced before regular driving. A seat that drops while driving can make you lose control.

issues.t: Loose steering and control arm fasteners (recall)
issues.sym: Clunks, wandering steering or looseness in the front end.
issues.why: Some fasteners on the steering parts or lower control arm ball joint may not have been tightened properly and could come apart.
issues.next: Check your VIN for the recall. If the front end feels loose, stop driving and have it towed in.

issues.sym: A vibration like rolling over rumble strips at steady speeds with light throttle, roughly highway and suburban speeds.
issues.why: The torque converter clutch shudders because the original transmission fluid absorbs moisture and breaks down. GM bulletins call for a full exchange to an updated fluid.
issues.next: Ask a dealer about bulletins 16-NA-175 and 18-NA-355 and the updated fluid exchange.

issues.t: Water in the trunk damaging the rear fuse block
issues.sym: No-start, a clicking or dead radio, a check engine light, random electrical faults, a damp trunk floor, and in rare cases smoke from the trunk.
issues.why: Water can get past the trunk lid seal, tail light pockets, rear window seams or drains and reach the rear fuse block and wiring. GM issued a bulletin on finding the leak, repairing the wiring and adding a trunk drain.
issues.next: If you see smoke or smell burning from the trunk, stop and shut the car off. Otherwise have the leak traced and the fuse block and battery cable checked for corrosion soon.

issues.t: Convertible top leaks at the windshield corner
issues.sym: Water drips in at the top corner of the windshield or the front pillar on convertibles.
issues.why: The front weatherstrip on the folding top can sit out of position at the corner.
issues.next: Ask a dealer about bulletin 16-NA-334, which repositions the weatherstrip.

issues.t: 10-speed automatic can lock the rear wheels (recall)
issues.sym: Harsh shifts or a sudden jolt and skid on a downshift; the rear wheels can briefly lock.
issues.why: Internal valve wear in the 10-speed automatic can damage the transmission. GM's fix adds software that watches for the wear and limits gear use.
issues.next: Check your VIN for this recall and have it done right away. If the transmission shifts harshly or jolts, limit driving until it is inspected.

issues.sym: A light knocking for the first few minutes after a cold start that fades as the engine warms up. Some engines also need oil topped up between changes, and a tired one may puff blue smoke at startup.
issues.why: Owners and engine specialists usually put the noise down to the pistons fitting a little loosely in the cylinders until they warm up and expand. It is widely reported on this engine and is often harmless.
issues.next: Check the oil level regularly and keep it topped up. If the knock does not go away when warm, or oil use climbs, have a shop do a compression or leak-down test.

issues.sym: Nothing is noticeable day to day. The risk only shows up if the driver airbag goes off in a crash.
issues.why: A manufacturing fault lets the inflator housing break apart when it fires, so metal pieces can be thrown into the cabin.
issues.next: Check the VIN with a Chevrolet dealer and have the free inflator replacement done before carrying passengers or driving much more.

issues.t: Steering wheel emblem can come loose in an airbag deployment (recall 21V-211)
issues.sym: You may notice the center emblem on the steering wheel sitting loose or lifting at an edge.
issues.why: The emblem is not bonded well enough to stay put when the driver airbag inflates, so it can be thrown at the driver.
issues.next: Have the VIN checked and the free recall repair done at your next convenient service visit.

issues.sym: A clunk or grinding from the rear, then the car losing drive even though the engine still runs.
issues.why: A retaining ring was left off the axle shaft on some cars, so the shaft can slide out of the differential.
issues.next: Stop driving and check the VIN for this recall. The axle is inspected and repaired free of charge.

issues.t: Fuel pump missing its pressure regulator can leak (recall 19V-837)
issues.sym: A strong fuel smell, a wet spot under the back of the car, or rough running and stalling.
issues.why: Some fuel pumps were built without the pressure regulator, so pressure climbs until the pump housing cracks and leaks.
issues.next: Stop driving, keep the car away from sparks and heat, and have the VIN checked. The pump is replaced free of charge.

issues.t: Seat belt anchor bolts may be the wrong ones (recall 20V-811)
issues.sym: Nothing shows up in normal use, and the belt latches and retracts as it should.
issues.why: Bolts of the wrong grade were used at a belt anchor, so the anchor may not hold the load of a crash.
issues.next: Check the VIN and have the free bolt replacement done before anyone relies on that belt.
